stage_a.note: Consistently enthusiastic, smiling broadly, and energetic throughout the presentation.
Highly animated with energetic gestures, showing clear excitement about the virtual wedding experience.
Very friendly and approachable, engaging the panel playfully with the cake and champagne.

venture.description: A virtual wedding production and live streaming service.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces Wedfuly, a virtual wedding production service, asking for $200k for 5 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 invites the panel to eat the cake and drink the champagne provided for them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 proposes a joke toast.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 joins the toast.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 drinks the champagne.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states he believes people will want to celebrate in person after the pandemic and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokes that they should take back S4's cake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 tells S4 he can enjoy the cake and champagne.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 shares a fun fact about the first wedding ever streamed online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses surprise.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 confirms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks how he knows that.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 explains he helped start the streaming industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges his background.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 adds that they did all the streaming at the time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if people will still want virtual weddings after the pandemic ends.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees but notes that 40 percent of their couples chose them because it fits their specific needs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how many weddings they have performed on the platform.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have performed 700 weddings since March 2020.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asserts that 700 weddings is nothing in the context of the broader wedding industry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks to finish explaining the statistic about the 40 percent of couples.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 allows her to continue, warning he will eviscerate her.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 enthusiastically agrees to continue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 tells them to wait.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if she was in the wedding business before and how she started this.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says her background is in software engineering.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 acknowledges the answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she was working at a big financial corporation as a software engineer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokes that they probably did not expect her to be a software engineer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 says she expected it because women can do anything.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees that women can do anything.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 affirms the statement.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she was looking for a female-dominated industry to use her degree, joking about S5 not fitting in.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 stares in response to the joke.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 laughs at the joke.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 agrees that S5 does not fit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 describes building an app for planners and realizing the traditional market ignored many couples' needs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how the process works after a customer signs up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the remote multimedia experience using low-tech equipment like cell phones and tripods.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how many weddings they can handle on a single Saturday.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies that they handled 30 weddings on one Saturday last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that their operations are built to easily scale up and scale back as needed.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what proprietary technology they actually developed, questioning if it is production or mixing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the tech lies in the planning process and data collection guide flow.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if they are a data company and what information they can get.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what data they aggregate and how deep their database is.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 agrees with S5's point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says they aggregate every detail about the wedding, including the guest list.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if they capture birth dates or attendee information.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they currently collect first name, last name, and email.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for their sales from the last year and year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says they have done a million dollars in sales since March 2020.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 is impressed by the sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 also expresses approval.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if they were profitable on that million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares revenue and profit figures for last year and this year, and average revenue per customer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what the profit margin is on their average customer package.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that it is 75 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if she has raised any outside money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms she owns 100 percent of the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 praises her for owning the whole company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 offers $200k for 20 percent, explaining he wants to use the data to feed his other wedding businesses.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges the explanation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 reiterates that is his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks him and says she is flattered.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters with $200k for 10 percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 refuses the counter, arguing he brings massive value and tracks the industry closely.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to explain her position.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 interrupts to speak.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 says she loves F1's story but it is not the right business for her, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S1.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 says F1 changed her life too.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses concern about scalability and lacking ancillary businesses, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S3.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 praises her as a great operator who will figure it out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states he will make an offer, recalling her counter to Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the terms of her counter.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 offers to do that deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts the offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes that S2 snatched it from Kevin.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 agrees.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 counts down and celebrates with confetti.

decisions.note: Believes people will want to celebrate in person post-pandemic and does not like the valuation.
Wants to use the venture as a data feeder business for his other wedding companies.
Loves her story and role model status but feels it is not the right business for her.
Concerned about scalability and lacks ancillary businesses to justify the investment.
Agrees to the exact terms F1 had countered to Kevin.
